cards.front: Mean
cards.back: Add up all the values and divide by how many values there are. Example: 4, 7, 9 has mean 20 ÷ 3.
cards.say: Mean. Add up all the values and divide by how many values there are. Example: four, seven, nine has mean twenty divided by three.

cards.front: Find the mean of 3, 4, 7, 9, 12
cards.back: 7. The total is 35 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
cards.say: Find the mean of three, four, seven, nine, twelve. seven. The total is thirty five and thirty five divided by five equals seven.

cards.front: Find the median of 3, 4, 7, 9, 12
cards.back: 7. It is the middle value when the numbers are in order.
cards.say: Find the median of three, four, seven, nine, twelve. seven. It is the middle value when the numbers are in order.

cards.front: Find the median of 2, 5, 6, 10
cards.back: 5.5. The middle numbers are 5 and 6, and halfway between them is 5.5.
cards.say: Find the median of two, five, six, ten. five point five. The middle numbers are five and six, and halfway between them is five point five.

cards.front: Find the mode of 4, 6, 6, 8, 9, 6, 4
cards.back: 6. It appears 3 times.
cards.say: Find the mode of four, six, six, eight, nine, six, four. six. It appears three times.

cards.front: Find the range of 12, 5, 19, 8
cards.say: Find the range of twelve, five, nineteen, eight. fourteen. nineteen minus five equals fourteen.

cards.front: The mean of 6 numbers is 8. What is their total?
cards.say: The mean of six numbers is eight. What is their total? forty eight. six times eight equals forty eight.

cards.front: The mean of 5 numbers is 9. Four of them total 38. Find the fifth.
cards.back: 7. The total is 5 × 9 = 45 and 45 - 38 = 7.
cards.say: The mean of five numbers is nine. Four of them total thirty eight. Find the fifth. seven. The total is five times nine equals forty five and forty five minus thirty eight equals seven.

cards.front: Which average is least affected by one very large value?
cards.back: The median. One extreme value can pull the mean up, but the median stays in the middle.
cards.say: Which average is least affected by one very large value? The median. One extreme value can pull the mean up, but the median stays in the middle.

cards.front: What is an outlier?
cards.back: A value that is much bigger or smaller than the rest of the data.
cards.say: What is an outlier? A value that is much bigger or smaller than the rest of the data.

cards.front: Why use the mode for the most popular shoe size?
cards.back: The mode is the most common value, so it shows which size sells most.
cards.say: Why use the mode for the most popular shoe size? The mode is the most common value, so it shows which size sells most.

cards.front: The probability scale goes from...
cards.back: 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
cards.say: The probability scale goes from... zero, impossible, to one, certain.

cards.front: If P(rain) = 0.3, what is P(no rain)?
cards.back: 0.7. The probabilities of all outcomes add up to 1, so 1 - 0.3 = 0.7.
cards.say: If the probability of rain is zero point three, what is the probability of no rain? Zero point seven. The probabilities of all outcomes add up to one.

cards.front: Probability of rolling more than 4 on a fair dice
cards.back: 2/6 = 1/3. The outcomes 5 and 6 are 2 out of 6.
cards.say: Probability of rolling more than four on a fair dice. two sixths equals one third. The outcomes five and six are two out of six.

cards.front: Probability of rolling a prime number on a fair dice
cards.back: 3/6 = 1/2. The primes are 2, 3 and 5.
cards.say: Probability of rolling a prime number on a fair dice. three sixths equals one half. The primes are two, three and five.

cards.front: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue counters. Probability of red as a fraction, decimal, percentage?
cards.say: A bag has four red and six blue counters. Probability of red as a fraction, decimal, percentage? two fifths, zero point four and forty per cent. four out of ten is two fifths.

cards.front: A spinner has 5 equal sections and 2 are red. Probability of red?
cards.say: A spinner has five equal sections and two are red. Probability of red? two fifths or zero point four.

cards.front: What does fair mean in probability?
cards.back: Every outcome is equally likely.
cards.say: What does fair mean in probability? Every outcome is equally likely.

cards.front: You roll a fair dice 60 times. About how many sixes do you expect?
cards.back: About 10. 1/6 of 60 = 10. The real result may differ.
cards.say: You roll a fair dice sixty times. About how many sixes do you expect? About ten. one sixth of sixty equals ten. The real result may differ.

cards.front: You flip a coin 100 times. About how many heads do you expect?
cards.back: About 50, but it will probably not be exactly 50.
cards.say: You flip a coin one hundred times. About how many heads do you expect? About fifty, but it will probably not be exactly fifty.

cards.front: 30 heads came up in 50 flips. What is the experimental probability of heads?
cards.say: Thirty heads came up in fifty flips. What is the experimental probability of heads? Thirty out of fifty, which is three fifths, or zero point six, or sixty per cent.

cards.front: What are mutually exclusive events?
cards.back: Events that cannot happen at the same time. Example: rolling an even number and rolling a 5.
cards.say: What are mutually exclusive events? Events that cannot happen at the same time. Example: rolling an even number and rolling a five.

cards.front: Two fair dice are rolled. Probability the total is 7?
cards.say: Two fair dice are rolled. Probability the total is seven? Six out of thirty six, which is one sixth. The ways are one and six, two and five, three and four, four and three, five and two, six and one.

cards.front: In a pie chart, what fraction is a 90 degree sector?
cards.back: 1/4, because 90 out of 360 is one quarter. That is 25%.
cards.say: In a pie chart, what fraction is a ninety degree sector? one quarter, because ninety out of three hundred and sixty is one quarter. That is twenty five per cent.

cards.front: 120 children. A pie chart shows 25% travel by bus. How many is that?
cards.say: one hundred and twenty children. A pie chart shows twenty five per cent travel by bus. How many is that? thirty. twenty five per cent of one hundred and twenty equals one hundred and twenty divided by four equals thirty.
